queries.title: create_projects_table
queries.description: Create the main projects table.
queries.sql:
create table public.projects (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  name text not null,
  symbol text not null default 'P',
  summary text not null default '',
  deadline date,
  progress smallint not null default 0 check (progress between 0 and 100),
  risk text not null default '',
  color text not null default '#4263eb',
  soft_color text not null default '#eef2ff',
  members text[] not null default '{}',
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

queries.title: create_profiles_table
queries.description: Create editable user profiles linked to Supabase Auth; passwords remain in auth.users.

queries.title: create_source_connections_table
queries.description: Create the non-secret Gmail and Google Calendar connection metadata table.
queries.sql:
create table public.source_connections (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  provider text not null check (provider in ('gmail', 'google_calendar')),
  provider_account_id text not null,
  account_email text not null,
  status text not null default 'active' check (status in ('active', 'expired', 'error', 'disconnected')),
  sync_cursor text,
  last_synced_at timestamptz,
  last_error text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (user_id, provider, provider_account_id)
);

queries.title: create_source_items_table
queries.description: Create the normalized upload, Gmail message, and Google Calendar event table.
queries.sql:
create table public.source_items (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  connection_id uuid references public.source_connections(id) on delete cascade,
  source_type text not null check (source_type in ('upload', 'gmail', 'google_calendar')),
  external_id text,
  external_thread_id text,
  title text not null default '',
  text_excerpt text not null default '' check (char_length(text_excerpt) <= 2000),
  extracted_text text,
  sender text,
  participants text[] not null default '{}',
  mime_type text,
  file_name text,
  storage_path text,
  source_url text,
  occurred_at timestamptz,
  ends_at timestamptz,
  location text,
  processing_status text not null default 'pending' check (processing_status in ('pending', 'processing', 'processed', 'failed')),
  processing_error text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  check ((source_type in ('gmail', 'google_calendar') and connection_id is not null and external_id is not null) or source_type = 'upload'),
  unique (connection_id, external_id)
);

queries.title: create_project_source_links_table
queries.description: Create the many-to-many source-to-project match table.
queries.sql:
create table public.project_source_links (
  id bigint generated by default as identity primary key,
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  project_id uuid not null references public.projects(id) on delete cascade,
  source_item_id uuid not null references public.source_items(id) on delete cascade,
  match_method text not null default 'ai' check (match_method in ('manual', 'rule', 'ai')),
  confidence numeric(5,4) check (confidence between 0 and 1),
  explanation text,
  review_status text not null default 'pending' check (review_status in ('pending', 'confirmed', 'rejected')),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (project_id, source_item_id)
);

queries.title: create_project_events_table
queries.description: Create the project timeline events table.
queries.sql:
create table public.project_events (
  id bigint generated by default as identity primary key,
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  project_id uuid not null references public.projects(id) on delete cascade,
  source_item_id uuid references public.source_items(id) on delete set null,
  event_type text not null check (event_type in ('email', 'file', 'meeting', 'decision', 'deadline', 'status', 'note')),
  title text not null,
  body text not null default '',
  person text not null default '',
  event_date timestamptz not null default now(),
  confidence numeric(5,4) check (confidence between 0 and 1),
  user_edited boolean not null default false,
  color text not null default '#4263eb',
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

queries.title: create_project_actions_table
queries.description: Create the extracted and manually entered project actions table.
queries.sql:
create table public.project_actions (
  id bigint generated by default as identity primary key,
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  project_id uuid not null references public.projects(id) on delete cascade,
  source_item_id uuid references public.source_items(id) on delete set null,
  title text not null,
  assignee text,
  due_date date,
  completed boolean not null default false,
  confidence numeric(5,4) check (confidence between 0 and 1),
  user_edited boolean not null default false,
  color text not null default '#4263eb',
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

queries.title: create_user_corrections_table
queries.description: Create the user confirmation and AI-correction audit table.
queries.sql:
create table public.user_corrections (
  id bigint generated by default as identity primary key,
  user_id uuid not null default auth.uid() references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  source_item_id uuid references public.source_items(id) on delete set null,
  project_id uuid references public.projects(id) on delete set null,
  correction_type text not null check (correction_type in ('confirm_match', 'reject_match', 'move_project', 'edit_event', 'edit_action')),
  previous_value jsonb,
  corrected_value jsonb,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

queries.title: create_source_secrets_table
queries.description: Create the backend-only, encrypted OAuth token table (RLS on, no policies).
queries.sql:
-- Store encrypted Google OAuth tokens for one source connection. Tokens are
-- encrypted at the application layer before insert, so this column holds only
-- ciphertext. This table is intentionally NOT exposed to the browser.
create table public.source_secrets (
  connection_id uuid primary key references public.source_connections(id) on delete cascade,
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  encrypted_token text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create index source_secrets_user_id_idx on public.source_secrets(user_id);

-- Enable Row Level Security but create NO policies on purpose. With RLS on and
-- zero policies, the browser publishable key (role 'authenticated') can never
-- read or write this table. Only the backend's direct Postgres connection,
-- which bypasses RLS, may access it.
alter table public.source_secrets enable row level security;

queries.title: check_source_secrets
queries.description: Verify source_secrets exists, has RLS enabled, and has NO policies (backend-only).
queries.sql:
with expected(table_name) as (values ('source_secrets'))
select
  e.table_name,
  case
    when c.oid is null then 'TABLE MISSING'
    when not c.relrowsecurity then 'RLS DISABLED (INSECURE)'
    when exists (
      select 1 from pg_catalog.pg_policies p
      where p.schemaname = 'public' and p.tablename = e.table_name
    ) then 'HAS POLICY (INSECURE - browser could read tokens)'
    else 'READY (backend-only, no browser access)'
  end as status
from expected e
left join pg_catalog.pg_class c
  on c.relname = e.table_name
 and c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
 and c.relkind = 'r';

queries.title: add_source_items_normalized_at
queries.description: Stage 2: add nullable normalized_at marker + a queue index for un-normalized pending rows.
queries.sql:
-- Marks when Stage 2 (extract & normalize) cleaned a row's text. NULL means
-- the row still needs normalization. Re-ingesting a changed item resets this
-- to NULL so it is re-normalized.
alter table public.source_items
  add column if not exists normalized_at timestamptz;

-- Partial index for the Stage 2 work queue: pending rows not yet normalized.
create index if not exists source_items_normalize_queue_idx
  on public.source_items(user_id)
  where processing_status = 'pending' and normalized_at is null;

queries.title: check_normalized_progress
queries.description: Stage 2 progress: count source items by normalized vs not, per status.
queries.sql:
select
  source_type,
  processing_status,
  count(*) filter (where normalized_at is not null) as normalized,
  count(*) filter (where normalized_at is null) as not_normalized,
  count(*) as total
from public.source_items
group by source_type, processing_status
order by source_type, processing_status;

queries.title: add_source_items_dedupe_fields
queries.description: Stage 3: add content_hash, include_in_grouping, exclusion_reason, deduped_at + queue index.
queries.sql:
-- Stage 3 (clean & deduplicate) output. include_in_grouping = false means the
-- row is kept and retrievable but held out of AI grouping; exclusion_reason
-- explains why ('duplicate' | 'recurring_instance' | 'noise'). deduped_at marks
-- that Stage 3 has processed the row (NULL = still queued).
alter table public.source_items
  add column if not exists content_hash text,
  add column if not exists include_in_grouping boolean not null default true,
  add column if not exists exclusion_reason text,
  add column if not exists deduped_at timestamptz;

-- Work queue for Stage 3: normalized rows not yet deduplicated.
create index if not exists source_items_dedupe_queue_idx
  on public.source_items(user_id)
  where processing_status = 'pending'
    and normalized_at is not null
    and deduped_at is null;

-- Ready-for-grouping set for Stage 4.
create index if not exists source_items_grouping_ready_idx
  on public.source_items(user_id)
  where deduped_at is not null and include_in_grouping;

queries.title: check_dedupe_progress
queries.description: Stage 3 progress: counts by include_in_grouping and exclusion_reason.
queries.sql:
select
  include_in_grouping,
  coalesce(exclusion_reason, '(included)') as reason,
  count(*) as items
from public.source_items
where deduped_at is not null
group by include_in_grouping, exclusion_reason
order by include_in_grouping desc, items desc;

queries.title: add_embeddings_and_relationships
queries.description: Stage 4: enable pgvector, add 384-dim embedding column + embedded_at, and create item_relationships (candidate pairs).

queries.title: check_stage4_progress
queries.description: Stage 4 progress: embedded vs not among included items, and relationship pair count.
queries.sql:
select
  (select count(*) from public.source_items
     where include_in_grouping and deduped_at is not null and embedding is not null) as embedded,
  (select count(*) from public.source_items
     where include_in_grouping and deduped_at is not null and embedding is null) as not_embedded,
  (select count(*) from public.item_relationships) as relationship_pairs;

queries.title: add_projects_origin
queries.description: Stage 5: mark whether a project was created by AI grouping ('ai') or by a user ('user'), so AI re-runs can be reset cleanly.

queries.title: check_grouping_progress
queries.description: Stage 5 progress: AI vs user projects, and source-item links by method/review status.
queries.sql:
select 'projects' as kind, origin as detail, count(*) as n
from public.projects group by origin
union all
select 'links', match_method || '/' || review_status, count(*)
from public.project_source_links group by match_method, review_status
order by kind, detail;

queries.title: add_source_items_extracted_at
queries.description: Stage 6: add extracted_at marker (NULL = still needs event/action extraction) + queue index.

queries.title: check_extract_progress
queries.description: Stage 6 progress: event/action counts per AI project.
queries.sql:
select p.symbol, p.name,
  count(distinct e.id) as events,
  count(distinct a.id) as actions
from public.projects p
left join public.project_events e on e.project_id = p.id
left join public.project_actions a on a.project_id = p.id
where p.origin = 'ai'
group by p.id, p.symbol, p.name
order by count(distinct e.id) + count(distinct a.id) desc;

queries.title: add_project_actions_status_backlog
queries.description: Stage 6 extension: AI-inferred status (drives the catch-up board's 4 columns) beyond today's boolean completed, plus a backlog flag.
queries.sql:
-- Stage 6 extension: real status beyond the boolean `completed`, so the
-- catch-up board (Not Started / In Progress / Completed / Backlog) can be a
-- pure read grouping. `backlog` marks AI-suggested-but-not-urgent actions.
alter table public.project_actions
  add column if not exists status text
    check (status in ('not_started', 'in_progress', 'completed')),
  add column if not exists backlog boolean not null default false;

-- Backfill existing rows from the boolean so nothing is left NULL.
update public.project_actions
set status = case when completed then 'completed' else 'not_started' end
where status is null;

alter table public.project_actions
  alter column status set default 'not_started',
  alter column status set not null;

queries.title: check_action_status_progress
queries.description: Stage 6 board data: action counts by status and backlog.
queries.sql:
select
  count(*) filter (where status = 'not_started') as not_started,
  count(*) filter (where status = 'in_progress') as in_progress,
  count(*) filter (where status = 'completed') as completed,
  count(*) filter (where backlog) as backlog
from public.project_actions;

queries.title: add_project_events_requires_response
queries.description: Stage 6 extension: explicit LLM-judged 'does this need a reply' signal, feeding Stage 7's waiting list and Stage 10's reply drafts.
queries.sql:
-- Stage 6 extension: explicit, LLM-judged "does this need a reply from the
-- user" signal. Replaces the old client-side statWaiting guess. NULL means
-- not yet classified (rows extracted before this column existed).
alter table public.project_events
  add column if not exists requires_response boolean;

queries.title: check_requires_response_progress
queries.description: Stage 6 progress: events classified as needing a reply, not needing one, or not yet classified.
queries.sql:
select
  count(*) filter (where requires_response is true) as requires_response,
  count(*) filter (where requires_response is false) as no_response_needed,
  count(*) filter (where requires_response is null) as not_yet_classified
from public.project_events;

queries.title: add_profiles_last_catchup_at
queries.description: Stage 7: each user's catch-up checkpoint, advanced when they view/dismiss the digest (not on every login).
queries.sql:
-- Stage 7: catch-up checkpoint. NULL = never caught up yet; Stage 7 falls
-- back to auth.users.last_sign_in_at in that case.
alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists last_catchup_at timestamptz;

queries.title: check_catchup_checkpoints
queries.description: Stage 7: each user's current catch-up checkpoint.
queries.sql:
select id, display_name, last_catchup_at, updated_at
from public.profiles
order by updated_at desc
limit 20;

queries.title: add_projects_catchup_summary
queries.description: Stage 7 digest: one Haiku-written sentence per project summarizing its recent activity, precomputed (not generated live at page load).
queries.sql:
-- Stage 7 digest summary. Precomputed server-side (backend/digest) so
-- opening the dashboard never makes a live LLM call. NULL until the first
-- run; catchup_summary_at lets the generator skip projects with no new
-- events since the last summary.
alter table public.projects
  add column if not exists catchup_summary text,
  add column if not exists catchup_summary_at timestamptz;

queries.title: check_catchup_summaries
queries.description: Stage 7 digest: which projects have a summary and how fresh it is.
queries.sql:
select symbol, name, catchup_summary, catchup_summary_at, updated_at
from public.projects
order by catchup_summary_at desc nulls first
limit 20;

queries.title: add_projects_category
queries.description: Stage 5: one LLM-classified category per project (project | meeting_series | training | conference | interview | admin), for digest tag pills.
queries.sql:
-- Stage 5 extension: a single domain category the namer (Sonnet 5)
-- assigns alongside name/summary/symbol. 'project' is the generic
-- default and is not surfaced as a tag in the UI -- only the more
-- specific categories are.
alter table public.projects
  add column if not exists category text
    check (category in ('project', 'meeting_series', 'training', 'conference', 'interview', 'admin'))
    not null default 'project';

queries.title: check_project_categories
queries.description: Stage 5: category distribution across a user's AI projects.
queries.sql:
select category, count(*) as projects
from public.projects
where origin = 'ai'
group by category
order by projects desc;

queries.title: add_project_events_issue_type
queries.description: Stage 6 extension: add 'issue' to project_events.event_type for blockers/risks/disagreements, feeding the digest and (later) board tag taxonomy (Task/Meeting/Decision/Issue-Blocker/Update).
queries.sql:
-- Previously blockers/risks/disagreements had no home and got folded
-- into 'decision' or 'note'. Adding a real type keeps the digest's
-- Issue/Blocker tag genuine rather than keyword-guessed, and gives the
-- same taxonomy a clean column to reuse on the board later.
alter table public.project_events drop constraint if exists project_events_event_type_check;
alter table public.project_events add constraint project_events_event_type_check
  check (event_type in ('email', 'file', 'meeting', 'decision', 'deadline', 'status', 'note', 'issue'));

queries.title: check_event_type_breakdown
queries.description: Stage 6: event counts by type, to confirm 'issue' is being classified.
queries.sql:
select event_type, count(*) as events
from public.project_events
group by event_type
order by events desc;

queries.title: check_event_source_dates
queries.description: Stage 6 debugging: every event next to its actual source message/event, to spot-check whether the AI-interpreted event_date agrees with when the source really occurred.
queries.sql:
select
  p.name as project,
  e.event_type,
  e.title as event_title,
  e.event_date,
  s.title as source_title,
  s.occurred_at as source_occurred_at,
  left(s.text_excerpt, 140) as source_excerpt
from public.project_events e
join public.projects p on p.id = e.project_id
left join public.source_items s on s.id = e.source_item_id
order by p.name, e.event_date desc;

queries.title: add_user_corrections_edit_project
queries.description: Stage 8: allow correcting a project's own summary -- edit_event/edit_action existed for those entities, but nothing covered the project-level summary shown on the project page.

queries.title: purge_all_source_content
queries.description: DESTRUCTIVE: delete ALL ingested Gmail/Calendar content and its derived rows (source_items, events, actions, links, relationships, projects). Keeps source_connections + source_secrets so you can re-sync.

queries.title: check_content_counts
queries.description: Row counts for the content tables (verify a purge left them empty).
queries.sql:
select 'source_items' as t, count(*) n from public.source_items
union all select 'project_events', count(*) from public.project_events
union all select 'project_actions', count(*) from public.project_actions
union all select 'project_source_links', count(*) from public.project_source_links
union all select 'item_relationships', count(*) from public.item_relationships
union all select 'projects', count(*) from public.projects
union all select 'source_connections', count(*) from public.source_connections
union all select 'source_secrets', count(*) from public.source_secrets
order by t;

queries.title: purge_tokens_and_disconnect
queries.description: DESTRUCTIVE: also delete the stored OAuth tokens and connections (full disconnect). Run purge_all_source_content first if you also want the content gone.
queries.sql:
delete from public.source_secrets;
delete from public.source_connections;

queries.title: create_mvp_indexes
queries.description: Create indexes used by user-scoped dashboard and processing queries.

queries.title: enable_mvp_row_level_security
queries.description: Enable Row Level Security on all seven application tables.

queries.title: create_mvp_owner_policies
queries.description: Create authenticated-user ownership policies for all seven application tables.

queries.title: check_all_tables
queries.description: Check that all MVP tables, including profiles, exist and have RLS and at least one policy.
queries.sql:
with expected_tables(table_name) as (
  values
    ('profiles'),
    ('projects'),
    ('source_connections'),
    ('source_items'),
    ('project_source_links'),
    ('project_events'),
    ('project_actions'),
    ('user_corrections')
)
select
  e.table_name,
  case
    when c.oid is null then 'TABLE MISSING'
    when not c.relrowsecurity then 'RLS DISABLED'
    when not exists (
      select 1
      from pg_catalog.pg_policies p
      where p.schemaname = 'public'
        and p.tablename = e.table_name
    ) then 'POLICY MISSING'
    else 'READY'
  end as status
from expected_tables e
left join pg_catalog.pg_class c
  on c.relname = e.table_name
 and c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace
 and c.relkind = 'r'
order by e.table_name;
